decision.summary: Tenant gave one month's notice, which is too short under the Renters' Rights Act. I told him the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026 and asked the landlord whether he will agree in writing to an earlier date. I added a note on the property and set a follow-up for 14 Oct.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date under current law?
answers.answer: No. One month is too short; two months' written notice is needed. Notice was given 10 Oct 2026, so the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: The landlord agrees in writing to a shorter notice period or a surrender by agreement, for example 10 Nov, or a date when a replacement tenant is found. It is the landlord's decision and the tenant has no right to it.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: I replied to the tenant explaining the two-month rule, that 10 Dec stands unless the landlord agrees otherwise, and that keys and deposit details will follow once the end date is confirmed. I asked the landlord for a decision, added a record note and scheduled a follow-up for 14 Oct.

actions_claimed.description: Asked landlord to decide on early end

conflicts: Tenant says one month's notice; the law requires two months, so the legal rule was applied.
assumptions: Notice was received 10 Oct 2026 and the two-month period runs from that date.
Rent stays due until the tenancy ends.

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and good luck with the new job.

Since 1 May 2026 a tenant needs to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Your email of 10 October means the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026, and you remain responsible for rent until then.

You can leave sooner only if your landlord agrees in writing. I'm asking him now whether he'd agree to 10 November, or another date. I can't promise he will, and until he does, 10 December stands. Please don't hand back keys or treat 10 November as agreed yet.

Keys: we'll confirm where and when to return them once the end date is settled. Please keep them until then.

Deposit: your £2,019 is held in the mydeposits scheme. It's returned after the tenancy ends and we've done a check-out and agreed any deductions. I can't give a date yet, but we'll explain the steps once your end date is confirmed.

You'll hear from us again by Wednesday 14 October.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
